scope: 01–28: discrete and continuous information theory, compression, channel coding, rate-distortion, and applications; base-2 logs unless stated

claims.statement: I(x)=-log2 p(x); entropy is average surprisal
Bayes theorem and Jensen inequality require their stated probability and positivity assumptions
Entropy for finite alphabets is concave and bounded above by log2 M; conditioning reduces entropy only on average; the discrete maximum entropy problem requires explicit constraints
claims.toy: X1 fair, X2=X1, X3 independent fair -> joint entropy=2 bits

claims.statement: For i.i.d. finite-alphabet sources -log2 P(X^n)/n converges in probability to entropy. Typical set high-probability and cardinality bounds are asymptotic.
For binary uniquely decodable source codes, H(X)<=L; Shannon prefix lengths ceil(-log2 p) achieve L<H+1; prefix lengths satisfy Kraft.
Huffman greedy merge produces minimum mean length among binary symbol-by-symbol prefix codes with known symbol weights.
Arithmetic encoding refines [L,U) using both new endpoints from old bounds, and exact dyadic inclusion allows a finite prefix; finite precision requires renormalization and termination protocol.
LZ77 copies from an already decoded sliding window and may overlap; LZ78 builds phrase indices; DEFLATE couples LZ77 matches and Huffman codes with a 32KiB history limit.
claims.toy: ABCABCABC -> literal A,B,C plus match(distance=3,length=6); LZ78 ABABABA -> A|B|AB|ABA

claims.statement: DMC channel kernels are conditional row-normalized matrices. BSC/BEC have distinct noise semantics and two independent BSCs cascade with epsilon=p+q-2pq.
claims.toy: BSC(.1) with uniform input I=.5310044; cascade BSC(.1),BSC(.2) => effective error .26

claims.statement: DMC capacity is max over input distributions, not mutual information at arbitrary prior; symmetric BSC/BEC admit closed forms and BA optimizes general finite channel capacity.
For stationary finite DMC, rate R<C admits a sequence of codes with vanishing average block error; weak converse via Fano and I(M;Y^n)≤nC forbids vanishing error for R>C.
claims.toy: BSC(.1) C≈.5310044; repetition n=3 p=.1: block error=.028 with rate=1/3

claims.statement: Hamming(7,4) with parity at positions 1,2,4 corrects one bit by s=Hr^T; 16 radius-one balls size 8 partition all 128 seven-bit vectors.

A cyclic code is a linear subspace closed under cyclic shift; it is generated by g(x) dividing x^n-1, and every codeword c(x)=m(x)g(x). CRC appends the remainder of d(x)x^r modulo g(x), so a received frame is a multiple of g(x) iff the error polynomial is divisible by g(x).
claims.toy: (7,4) g=1+x+x^3: m=1011 -> 1111111; CRC r=3 g=1011: d=1101 -> remainder 001, frame 1101001; CRC-32 check 123456789 -> reflected 0xCBF43926, non-reflected 0xFC891918

claims.statement: A rate-1/2 K=3 convolutional encoder (g0=111, g1=101) is a 4-state finite-state machine; Viterbi decoding keeps one minimum-metric survivor per state and runs in O(T*2^(K-1)).
claims.toy: msg 1011 + tail 00 -> 1110 0001 0111; flipping any single output bit still decodes to 101100

claims.statement: Perfect secrecy is P(M=m|C=c)=P(M=m), equivalently H(M|C)=H(M) and I(M;C)=0. For c=m XOR k with uniform independent key it holds; Shannon proved it forces H(K)>=H(M). Reusing a pad key leaks c1 XOR c2 = m1 XOR m2.
claims.toy: m=[1,0,1,1], k=[0,1,1,0] -> c=[1,1,0,1]; reuse: c1 XOR c2 = m1 XOR m2 independent of k

claims.statement: R(D)=min_{p(xhat|x): E[d]<=D} I(X;Xhat) is non-increasing and convex; R(0)=H(X) for discrete sources, R(D)=0 for D>=Dmax. Gaussian with squared error: R(D)=0.5*log2(sigma^2/D) for 0<D<=sigma^2. Parallel components use reverse water-filling.
